This includes orders placed using offline payment methods'; and the same Offline Payment Methods page has Bank Deposit let customers 'make a payment directly into your bank account'. what: The record leaves out two limits its source puts on it: the page's title is 'Transactions API (Beta)', and the page sends the reader elsewhere 'For supported providers, payment methods, and detailed usage instructions'. That guide (held, 2026-10-12) says 'Initially, this API supports importing transactions from the following payment providers: Adyen, Authorize.net, BigCommerce Payments, Braintree, PayPal Commerce Platform, Stripe' and 'The following payment methods are supported: ACH (Adyen, Braintree, and Stripe only), Apple Pay, Credit Card, Google Pay, iDEAL, PayPal (...)'; 'these providers must first be configured on the merchant's store using the same credentials as those being used to process payments externally.' So line 22, 'Shopify and BigCommerce keep that payment as a transaction on the order', where 'that payment' is one the seller records by hand as received outside the platform (line 20), says more than the source: the API is for payments processed externally through those providers, for 'post-order actions such as capture, void, and refund', not for an offline payment the merchant received. Lines 69, 88 and 100 are the design's and say nothing of BigCommerce; the coordinator may weigh that the record shows import from six named providers, not entry by a bank feed, invoicing tool or courier.
fix: Record scope: 'Beta; payments processed externally through the supported providers (Adyen, Authorize.net, BigCommerce Payments, Braintree, PayPal Commerce Platform, Stripe) and payment methods (ACH, Apple Pay, Credit Card, Google Pay, iDEAL, PayPal)'. Line 22: drop BigCommerce from 'keep that payment as a transaction on the order', or say 'BigCommerce's Transactions API (Beta) creates transaction records for payments processed externally through supported providers'.
